svg.title: mcraw4vulkan — from RAW recording to output
svg.desc: A left-to-right diagram of the main production image and audio pathways. The .mcraw file has separate metadata, image payload, and audio payload rectangles. The CPU reads camera and frame settings, reads frame data, and prepares decoding. The GPU decodes raw sensor pixels, then the selected workflow follows one of three branches. Display optionally corrects lens shading, rebuilds color, and presents the image on the GPU. DNG optionally corrects lens shading while retaining the raw sensor mosaic, transfers the pixels to the CPU, and packages raw pixels with camera metadata as virtual DNG frames on demand. PIPE prepares linear raw values, optionally corrects lens shading, reconstructs color, converts and packs 12-bit scene-linear YUV on the GPU, then transfers frames to the CPU for writing to a stream or file. Blue outlines and arrows represent CPU image work; green represents GPU work. Dashed blue arrows carry image settings and metadata. Gray outlines and arrows represent CPU audio work. When audio is present, the CPU reads recorded samples and track details. Display aligns the sound to video timing and plays it when sound is enabled. DNG and PIPE package the original recorded samples as WAV: a virtual audio file beside the DNG images or a separate audio file beside PIPE video. Audio is not embedded in DNG images or in the raw video stream. Solid arrows carry image or audio data, with arrow color following the stage supplying it. Each output is a separate workflow, not a simultaneous fan-out. CPU image decoding and small supporting operations are omitted.

g.text: From a RAW recording to playback, RAW frames, or an editing stream
Image pixels stay on the GPU through playback.
RAW sensor data stays available for development in your editor.
Scene-linear video for grading; add exposure and a viewing transform.
Main production path · Each workflow follows its own branch · CPU decoding omitted
Lens correction defaults: Display off · DNG / PIPE on
